facts.statement: The genus Enseosteus was first described by Jaeckel in 1919.
The type species of the genus is Enseosteus jaekelli.
Ottonosteus jaekeli is listed as a synonym of Enseosteus.
Enseosteus is classified as a small selenosteid arthrodire placoderm.
facts.quote: Enseosteus is an extinct genus of small selenosteid arthrodire placoderms

facts.statement: Fossils of Enseosteus have been found in the Upper Frasnian Kellwasserkalk facies of Germany and Morocco.
facts.quote: known from the Upper Frasnian Kellwasserkalk facies of Late Devonian Germany and Morocco

facts.statement: The type species E. jaekelli is distinguished by a bulbous, knob-shaped rostrum.
facts.quote: the type species, E. jaekelli, has a bulbous, knob-shaped rostrum

facts.statement: It is debated whether the genus Walterosteus should be synonymized with Enseosteus, as Rücklin (2011) rejects this classification despite Denison's earlier proposal.
facts.quote: Rücklin (2011) agrees with Denison's synonymizing of Ottonosteus, but rejects Denison's synonymization of Walterosteus

facts.statement: Enseosteus lived during the Frasnian stage, between 382.31 and 372.15 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Frasnian to Frasnian (382.31 to 372.15 million years ago)

facts.statement: Enseosteus belongs to the family Selenosteidae.
Enseosteus is a member of the class Placodermi.
